venue.name: Sooke Region Museum
venue.description: The Sooke Region Museum and Visitor Centre sits on Phillips Road in Sooke and tells the story of the region. Indoor exhibits cover First Nations basketry, mining, forestry and maritime history, along with the All Sooke Day film. Outdoor exhibits on the grounds include the Forestry Path, the Servants Quarters, Moss Cottage and the lighthouse from Triangle Island. Museum entrance is by donation and the grounds are open during daylight hours.

facility_notes.bus_parking: The Sooke Region Museum and Visitor Centre has several areas for visitors to park and all of the parking is free. Nothing is said about where a bus goes.

venue.hours_notes: September to May the museum is open Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday 9:30am to 5pm and Wednesday 10:00am to 5pm. Closed Sunday and Monday. Museum entrance is by donation. The grounds are open during daylight hours only.
venue.seasonal_notes: School tours run in two sessions each school year, one in the fall and one in the spring. The spring 2026 dates are full and bookings for the fall tours in November and December open in September 2026.

programs.name: School tour
programs.description: A station based morning tour for Kindergarten to Grade 8, built around the BC Curricular Competencies. Kindergarten to Grade 5 classes do four 15 minute activities plus a 30 minute block where they cook bannock in the fireplace and eat the snacks they have brought. Grades 6, 7 and 8 do four 30 minute activities, one of which is bannock plus making camas seed balls. Teachers choose the other activities on the booking form from a list that includes Art Inspired by the Land, butter making, hand washing clothes, Moss Cottage, tracks and scat, the Triangle Island lighthouse, artifact detectives, forestry, spinning and sequencing archival photographs. The museum takes two classes per visit. A visit costs $200. If you are only booking one class, the discount code Single Class brings it to $100, and the code is case sensitive. Chaperones and teachers are not charged. Students should arrive organised into 5 or 6 groups with name tags, and each activity group is kept to a maximum of 8 children.
programs.what_children_do: Move round the museum and grounds in small groups of about eight, spending 15 or 30 minutes at each station. They cook bannock over the fire in the stone fireplace and eat it with jam, shake cream into butter and taste it, wash clothes by hand, press flowers or print tree rings, handle real artifacts and work out what they were for, use hand carders and drop spindles on wool, and walk the Forestry Path outside. In Moss Cottage the younger ones are met by a costumed Aunt Tilly who talks about life in Sooke in 1902.
programs.our_note: The $200 is for the visit, not per child, and it covers two classes, so it is cheap if you can fill it and worth splitting with another class. If you are bringing one class on your own, the single class code drops it to $100. It runs 9:45 to noon and the children bring their own snacks, so plan lunch for after you get back.
programs.practical_summary: Free parking on site and a mix of indoor rooms and outdoor grounds. Washrooms, an indoor space to eat and what happens in heavy rain are not mentioned on the site, so those are worth a call before you confirm.
programs.payment_timing: Payment can be made at the time of booking by credit card, or at the time of visit by cheque or cash.
programs.evidence: Cost $200 per visit. No charge for chaperones and teachers.

programs.name: Group visit
programs.description: Outside the school tour sessions, a group can come during opening hours. Museum entrance is by donation and no group rate is published. Tours inside Moss Cottage or the Triangle Island Lighthouse can be added to a group booking, but the site does not say what those cost or how long they take. The rates document the site links to did not open, so ask for current figures.
programs.what_children_do: Look round the indoor exhibits on First Nations basketry, mining, forestry and maritime history, watch the All Sooke Day film, and walk the grounds where the Forestry Path, the Servants Quarters and the Triangle Island lighthouse are laid out.
programs.our_note: This is the option if your group is outside Kindergarten to Grade 8 or you have missed the two booking sessions. Nothing about price, group size or notice is published for it, so treat one phone call as part of the plan. Ask at the same time whether Moss Cottage and the lighthouse will be open, since those are only unlocked for booked groups.
programs.practical_summary: Parking is free and the grounds are open in daylight. Washrooms, somewhere to eat and a rain plan are not mentioned, and neither is a price for groups, so call before you commit a date.
programs.evidence: If your group would like to see inside Moss Cottage or Triangle Island Lighthouse, tours can be added for group bookings.

images.alt: A gravel path between a weathered timber cabin with a wooden staircase and a row of white pop up tents with tables of goods, with tall conifers behind and a few people walking through.

A group of about six children and two adults standing outdoors on gravel in front of a large rusted machine with a cable drum, sheltered under an open timber frame roof, with a big cut log in the foreground.
Three children seen from behind standing at a large stone fireplace with a wood fire burning in it, holding sticks out over the flames.
